entries.topic: Policy instruments and land held, added to the network map (Nov 2026)

claims.text: JNF holdings 22,363 dunams (1920), 516,000 (1940), 936,000 (May 1948); Jews owned only about 7% of the land of Palestine before 1948.

About 450,000 dunams bought before 1917; about 2 million by May 1948; JNF acquired 390,000 dunams in 1940-46, 238,000 from Arabs; the 1940 regulations (Zone A 63%, Zone B 32%, free zone 5%) widely circumvented; the UN partition map substantially mirrors concentrations of Jewish land purchase.
Sursock family sales of about 240,000 dunams (Shaw Commission table), 1,746 families displaced; 1921-25 about 80,000 acres to the American Zion Commonwealth.
1940 Land Transfers Regulations: Zone A transfers to non-Arabs prohibited; Zone B require High Commissioner's sanction; no restriction elsewhere, including municipal areas.
MacDonald letter, 13 Feb 1931, to Weizmann, considered a withdrawal of the Passfield White Paper; reaffirmed support for continued immigration and land purchase.
June 1922 White Paper: 'as of right and not on the sufferance'; immigration not to exceed the economic capacity of the country to absorb new arrivals.
Permanent Mandates Commission, report public 18 Aug 1939: four of seven voting members could not find the White Paper in conformity with the Mandate.
JTA 4 Nov 1934: PICA owns in Palestine about half a million dunams.
